Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7975); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem:--Siloam.
BiblicalUsage: Siloam was the pool of Jerusalem where Jesus sent the blind man to wash, and the man went and washed and came seeing. The same name marks the tower that fell and slew eighteen, and Jesus asked whether those eighteen were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pool of Siloam is where obedience and sight meet, because the blind man was healed on the way to the water, not before it.
RelatedEvents: The Healing of the Man Born Blind
